name: Atmospheric CO₂
summary: CO₂ 428.6 ppm at Mauna Loa, up 3.36 ppm on a year, above the 3 ppm Alert line
state: Mauna Loa recorded 428.57 ppm in the week of 1 Nov, 3.36 ppm higher than a year earlier and above the 3 ppm per year Alert line (NOAA GML). Weekly growth figures are noisy, so one reading can move the rate noticeably. The weekly level has risen from 425.91 ppm over the past eight readings.
for_you: CO₂ growth is a slow indicator of long-term warming rather than an immediate hazard. It shapes climate risk over decades.
rubric_hit: Alert: year-on-year growth 3.36 ppm > 3.0 ppm line (week of 1 Nov)

sources.title: NOAA GML — Trends in atmospheric CO₂, Mauna Loa weekly

why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.
